"All" and "Alerts" controls, follow the ARIA Tabs pattern (the container should have a role=tablist, each button role=tab with aria-selected, each associated view to be role=tabpanel with aria-labelledby set to the ID of its corresponding tab (All or Alerts); keyboard navigation between tabs is via Left/Right arrows)

@Ryan Casey Hi, Ryan, FYI: this color combo is slightly below the WCAG 2.2 threshold for regular text:
* Foreground: #FAFBFE
* Background: #E2274F

This screen looks good to me from an accessibility standpoint, provided the tab focus order is as you'd expect. Labels look clear, contrast looks appropriate. If the "Country" and "State" dropdowns aren't standard select elements, then I'd just suggest using aria-expanded on them to indicate state (for screen reader users in particular).

I think we should consider a couple aspects of contrast here: (1) the contrast between the background of the dialog and the changed-info highlighting, and (2) the contrast between the changed-info text color and the existing-info text color. The contrast between the changed-info highlighting and the changed-info text is sufficient.

For (1), the contrast ratio between the highlight (#E6F0FC) and the background (#FFFFFF) is 1.2:1 - people in very bright environments or who have contrast loss would have a hard time telling that there's a different background. For (2), the contrast ratio between the changed-info text color (#0252BF) and the existing-info text color (#15141A) is 2.6:1. Both of these ratios are insufficient for AA, making it tough to distinguish when not in high contrast mode.

I don't want to prescribe a design, but we do want to (1) maintain at least a 3:1 contrast ratio between the highlight and the background so people can see the highlight, (2) have similarly high contrast between the regular text and the changed-info text, and (3) have high contrast between the highlight and the changed-info text. We might be able to take a page from the HCM mockup's book and make the highlighting #0252BF and the text color #FFFFFF. Alternately, you could add some other indicator other than color to distinguish changed text, such as italicization.
For properties on these cancel options, you might want to add "aria-haspopup" to indicate to assistive technologies that the button spawns a popup when clicked.

This screen looks good to me from an accessibility standpoint, provided the tab focus order is as you'd expect. Labels look clear, contrast looks appropriate. If the "Country" and "State" dropdowns aren't standard select elements, then I'd just suggest using aria-expanded on them to indicate state (for screen reader users in particular).

I think we should consider a couple aspects of contrast here: (1) the contrast between the background of the dialog and the changed-info highlighting, and (2) the contrast between the changed-info text color and the existing-info text color. The contrast between the changed-info highlighting and the changed-info text is sufficient.

For (1), the contrast ratio between the highlight (#E6F0FC) and the background (#FFFFFF) is 1.2:1 - people in very bright environments or who have contrast loss would have a hard time telling that there's a different background. For (2), the contrast ratio between the changed-info text color (#0252BF) and the existing-info text color (#15141A) is 2.6:1. Both of these ratios are insufficient for AA, making it tough to distinguish when not in high contrast mode.

I don't want to prescribe a design, but we do want to (1) maintain at least a 3:1 contrast ratio between the highlight and the background so people can see the highlight, (2) have similarly high contrast between the regular text and the changed-info text, and (3) have high contrast between the highlight and the changed-info text. We might be able to take a page from the HCM mockup's book and make the highlighting #0252BF and the text color #FFFFFF. Alternately, you could add some other indicator other than color to distinguish changed text, such as italicization.
For properties on these cancel options, you might want to add "aria-haspopup" to indicate to assistive technologies that the button spawns a popup when clicked.
